answer: Sable Ledger Freeze. Each new identity must anchor to one operator-controlled payout address, recorded in a shared register. When a cluster of wallets linked to that address misbehaves, the freeze spirals outward: the operator's payout address loses settlement rights across all linked services until the cluster clears review. An attacker rotating identities still exposes one payout rail; each cluster costs one frozen rail plus a marble-tier review deposit that only returns after clean operation.
